g.text: BCL1213 | OPERATING SYSTEMS
Chapters 1–4 · reviewed exam revision sheet · 9 November 2026
1 OS FUNDAMENTALS
OS: manages CPU time, memory, devices, files and protection.
Batch: queued jobs | Time-sharing: interactive CPU time slices
Multiprogramming: run another ready job during an I/O wait.
Real-time: timing requirements matter; hard deadlines are mandatory.
Application → OS services / drivers → hardware
2 PROCESSES & SCHEDULING
New → Ready → Running → Terminated
Running → Waiting: blocks for I/O/event; Waiting → Ready: event completes
Running → Ready: preemption | Ready → Running: dispatch
PCB: PID, state, saved counter/registers, scheduling, memory and I/O info
Turnaround = completion − arrival | Response = first start − arrival
Waiting = turnaround − CPU burst (single-burst / no-I/O exercises)
FCFS: arrival order | SJF: shortest ready burst | RR: time quantum
3 MEMORY MANAGEMENT
Registers → Cache → RAM → Secondary storage
Generally: slower access and larger capacity as you move right.
Paging: fixed-size pages map to equal-size physical frames.
Physical address = frame × page size + offset; 0 ≤ offset < page size
Segmentation: variable logical regions; check 0 ≤ offset < limit.
Then physical address = segment base + offset.
Internal fragmentation: waste inside blocks; external: scattered holes.
4 SYNCHRONIZATION & DEADLOCKS
Race condition: timing/order of shared-state access changes the result.
Mutex: exclusive owner | Semaphore: available permits / signaling
Condition wait: releases mutex, blocks, reacquires; recheck in a loop.
Deadlock needs: mutual exclusion + hold and wait
+ no preemption + circular wait.
Prevention: break a necessary condition; a global lock order breaks cycles.
Concurrency may interleave on one core; parallelism executes at once.
Use with the full study guide, 40-question quiz and 76 flashcards.
Check arrival times, quantum, priority convention, address units and offset bounds.
